rubric_items.reason: All eight ticket acceptance criteria map to REQ-1..REQ-14; the URL pre-fill and fee-load-failure gaps were asked and answered (A-01, A-02); out-of-scope items carry reasons.

Most REQs are atomic with checkable conditions (e.g. 150000 paise -> Rs 1,500.00, 0 -> 0.00). REQ-12 'rest of the page is unchanged' is a broad catch-all that overlaps REQ-8/REQ-11 and is hard to test precisely.
Every known status cites a ticket line, the baseline, or a user answer; REQ-9 assumption was confirmed in A-02 and REQ-10 decided by A-01. Nothing invented.
No clash between ticket and baseline found: display-only fee, INR currency and paise storage agree with baseline constraints and glossary; booking rules and data protection preserved.
Two minimal, non-redundant questions with real options, answered by the user; neither is answered by the context pack.
Plain and consistent glossary use; small traceability slip where the Summary cites C1/C2 for the user story motive, and a glossary note is filed under Out of scope.

findings.text: The Summary cites C1 and C2 (paise storage, INR currency) as the basis for staff wanting to tell the patient the cost; those claims do not state that motive. The ticket story line does.

cites.quote: so they can tell the patient the cost before confirming (C1, C2)

so
that I can tell the patient what the visit will cost before I confirm it.

findings.suggested_fix: Cite the ticket story (ticket.md#L12-L13) for the motive and keep C1/C2 for the paise/INR facts.

findings.text: REQ-12 is a catch-all ('rest of the page is unchanged') that overlaps REQ-8 and REQ-11 and gives a tester no concrete condition to check.

cites.quote: Apart from the fee, the rest of the book appointment page is unchanged.
The slot list, booking rules and the rest of the page are unchanged.

findings.suggested_fix: Name the existing fields/controls that must stay the same (Doctor, Patient, date, slot list, Book button) so the check is concrete.

findings.text: A glossary note ('Consultation fee' is not a glossary term) is listed under Out of scope; it is not a scope exclusion and belongs with the glossary entries.

cites.quote: "Consultation fee" is not a glossary term; the Paise entry covers fees (C3), so no new term is needed.

findings.suggested_fix: Move the note to a glossary remark or drop it from Out of scope.
